decisions.statement: A verdict is one check's rather than one audit run's.
A check has one verdict, and it is the last verdict taken.
A verdict states the newest commit its finding still answers for.
A verdict states the moment the check ran.
A verdict is measured where the check ran, whatever that check refused.
A verdict is clean where the check ran and refused nothing.
A clean verdict answers for the commit it states and every ancestor of that commit.
Whether one commit is an ancestor of another is asked of git.
A verdict is kept in the repository whose audits take it.
A check's verdict is kept beside that check's page rather than beside the rest.
A verdict rides the audit log row the run that took it writes.
The row a verdict rides is composed here and written by whoever takes it.
A check's verdict is the one on the newest row of its audit log stating a commit.
A row stating no commit is a cost alone, and the reader walks past it.
A row that will not parse is read as no verdict rather than throwing.
The newest numbered file of the log is read first, and the one before it after.
A verdict no run took states the commit it answers for and no elapsed time.
A row states the refusal texts under `refused` beside their count under `refusals`.
An audit log is appended to and swept on a window, so an unbounded row fills it.
A refusal text is held to four thousand characters.
A row's refusal texts are held to a hundred and twenty thousand bytes.
One check now holds two hundred and twelve thousand bytes in one refusal.
Another holds forty-three thousand bytes over a hundred and seventy-one.
The texts ceiling is above what every check now refusing produces.
A refusal left off the row would read as new again every round after.
A text cut short says how many characters and lines went.
A row that left refusals off says how many there were in all.
No answer drawn from a row reads as whole where that row cut something.
A commit git will not name reads as no commit, and the row carries the cost alone.
Nothing here runs an audit.
Nothing here says which checks are owed a verdict.
Nothing here holds the file against a second writer.

definition: what a check's last audit found, and the commits that finding answers for
